The first of the Indian Institutes of Technology, founded in 1951 at Kharagpur in West Bengal. It started in the buildings of the Hijli Detention Camp, where the British had held freedom fighters.

A committee led by N. R. Sarkar had recommended in 1946 a set of higher technical institutes on the model of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, to train the engineers a free India would need. Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru backed the plan as part of his vision of modern science and industry. Parliament made the IITs institutes of national importance in 1956, and new ones followed at Bombay, Madras, Kanpur and Delhi, each helped by a foreign partner.

Entry by a hard national exam made the IITs famously selective. Their graduates built Indian industry and agencies such as ISRO, and many went to the United States, where they became leading figures in Silicon Valley and business. The IITs helped India's later software boom, led by firms like Infosys. Today there are more than twenty IITs.
